hard-law-order (1)

›hard_law_order
CANONICAL SEALED
category: hard-law-order
the structural, non-advisory order in which candidate actions are filtered before the entity constitution ever ranks them
1. HARD SAFETY LAW (world laws flagged safety=true; constitution cannot influence this gate — runs on world law + context only). 2. WORLD LAW (world_constitution.evaluate). 3. AUTHORITY (entity's authority envelope). 4. CAPABILITY (entity's declared capability set). 5. ENTITY CONSTITUTION RANKING (values/priorities/weights score surviving lawful candidates; may also REFUSE or emit NEED). Personal values can therefore NEVER create authority, override hard safety law, expand capability, or rewrite world law: unlawful candidates never reach ranking.

›request-vs-delivery

source: ~/workspace/funnel-docs/pulse-dev-hideout/parts/hideout-ops.js:59 (PAGE0_TEXT, REQUEST VS DELIVERY section)
›single overlay authority
CANONICAL
category: LAW
Only one manager may own global overlay placement and focus; overlays never fight for top-left, bottom dock, right edge, the fullscreen layer, or z-index.
source: bassseamoor/render-queue@main/abandoned-cathedral.html:8569
›overlay conflict rule
CANONICAL
category: LAW
Never two fullscreen layers at once, never two overlays holding the same region. A conflicting request is QUEUED (FIFO) — never silently dropped, never fought over.
source: bassseamoor/render-queue@main/abandoned-cathedral.html:8569
related: queued
›monitor law
CANONICAL
category: LAW
The six monitors are general control surfaces. No tool permanently owns a monitor unless the owner pins it. Flow: SELECT OBJECT → OPEN CONTROL PANEL → CHOOSE MONITOR.
source: bassseamoor/render-queue@main/abandoned-cathedral.html:8802
›spatial surface law
CANONICAL
category: LAW
A CONTROL SURFACE is separate from an OUTPUT/PROJECTION SURFACE, but both reference the same canonical object. Changing the control changes the one canonical thing; every projection updates.
source: bassseamoor/render-queue@main/abandoned-cathedral.html:8802
›real data only
CANONICAL
category: LAW
The blueprint library shows the real inventory; no decorative entries.

source: ~/workspace/funnel-docs/pulse-dev-hideout/parts/hideout-amend1.js:15
›routing law
CANONICAL
category: LAW
Old routes redirect / open the Hideout object-or-tool in context / honest unavailable. ?tool=X places the tool's control surface on a monitor; ?view=map|blueprints opens the room in that mode.

category: LAW
